card.name: Nijemo Kolo
card.tagline: Silent circle dance of the Dalmatian hinterland.
card.profile: A closed-circle couple dance from the Dalmatian hinterland (Dalmatinska zagora) of southern Croatia, performed essentially without musical accompaniment - the rhythm set by the dancers' steps. Male dancers lead female partners in vigorous, spontaneous, seemingly rule-free steps that publicly test the woman's skill; the lead is the kolovoda. It may be framed by ojkanje, rera or ganga singing or the diple (twin-reed shepherd's flute). Danced at fairs, weddings, carnivals and saint's-day celebrations (English Wikipedia; UNESCO).
card.insight: Inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List in 2011 (file 00359); its silence may have originated as a way for peasants to dance despite prohibitions, the rhythmic thumping of shoes itself a form of defiance (UNESCO).
